analysis:
This batch is documentation only: docs/developer/test.md (new Gemma 4 tensor-parallel test section; supplied excerpts at lines 1845-2653 are unchanged surrounding text, with the changed head range at 1231-1345 only partially visible in the patch excerpt) and docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (date bump, a tensor-parallel model/placement table, and a sentence on Gemma sliding-window prefix restore under tensor parallel). No executable code, key handling, attestation, authorization, or cache implementation is modified, so no control is weakened.

Relevant threat: T-041 (prefix cache, encrypted SSD tier, TTFT oracle). two-mac-cluster.md lines ~484-490 now say Gemma 4 sliding-window frontiers are kept in tensor parallel too, each Mac keeping its own half of the heads, with restore only when both Macs hold the prefix. This describes the implementation of cluster prefix caching, which is not in this PR's supplied evidence. I cannot verify that the underlying Gemma TP code preserves tenant/salt partitioning and HMAC-keyed names. The existing test table (test.md ~2284-2305) covers tenant partitioning for other families, but the Gemma TP prefix path is not named there. The next pass should confirm that the Gemma TP prefix code in the corresponding source PR is covered by the prefix tenant partition checks and does not widen the T-041 at-rest or cross-tenant exposure.

The docs claim only synthetic, loopback, single-Mac tests and explicitly disclaim real-weight numerics, pair qualification and speed, which is consistent with the threat model's no-overclaim posture (T-056). The documented 'DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_BATCH_LANES' setting and the planner's 'predicted faster' placement are availability/performance matters, not security regressions. I identified no findings. Uncertainty is limited to the unseen source for Gemma TP prefix storage.
